expectations.text: A file named library-loans.design.json sits next to the spec, has the fields spec, focus, equivalence_classes, boundary_values, state_transitions, tests and unknowns, and passes check_design.mjs.

The 7-day and 28-day loan period boundaries have inclusive: null, the boundary values 7 and 28 are expected unknown (6 and 29 invalid, 8 and 27 valid), and unknowns asks whether 'between 7 and 28' includes the ends.
expectations.evidence: BV-04/BV-05 inclusive null, 7 and 28 unknown, 6/29 invalid, 8/27 valid; U-06 asks

expectations.text: Boundaries the text does settle are marked from its words: age 'at least 12' (11 invalid, 12 valid, 13 valid), books 'up to 5' (5 valid, 6 invalid) and fines 'exceed 5.00 EUR' with a 0.01 EUR step (5.00 can borrow, 5.01 cannot).
expectations.evidence: Age 11/12/13 and fines 4.99/5.00/5.01 are right, but BV-02 'up to 5 books' is inclusive null with 5 books unknown (over-correction from the new 'up to' rule)

expectations.text: Matrix cells the spec neither lists nor forbids (for example renew from any state, or return from LOST) are marked unknown, not illegal, and are explained in unknowns, since the spec has no 'any other transition is forbidden' rule.
expectations.evidence: 'member renews the loan' is now an action; all 12 unlisted cells (incl. renew in every state and return from LOST) are unknown

expectations.text: The design does not invent error codes, messages or HTTP statuses for violations; unknowns asks what the system returns when a rule is broken.
expectations.evidence: No codes invented; U-02/04/05/07/10 ask what the system returns

expectations.text: The design does not present empty, null, negative or wrong-type inputs as spec-defined classes; it asks about them in unknowns.
expectations.evidence: No null/empty classes; questions in U-02 and U-07
